answer: A bonded stake makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit that is slashed if it cheats, so spawning thousands of copies costs thousands of deposits. Like a terrace rising step by step, trust is earned gradually as the stake stays locked through honest work, and at dawn of each new epoch the system checks that every identity still holds its bond. A sable ledger of slashing records makes repeat offenders visible, so an attacker cannot quietly reset and try again — each new identity starts from zero and pays full price.
